question: Which Article of the Constitution of India lays down the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as 250?
solution:
The correct answer is "**Article 80**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to** Article 80** of the Constitution, the **Rajya Sabha** can have a **maximum** of **250 members**, of which **12** are chosen **by** the **President** and 238 are elected by the States and the two Union Territories.
 
• The **formation** of the **Council of States** is outlined in **Article 80** of the Indian Constitution. Article 80 specifies the members of the Council of States as follows:
 
 
• The** President** will propose twelve candidates for **membership**. People with unique **knowledge** or real-world experience in the following sectors, notably literature, science, art, and social service, are to be** nominated** as members by the President.
 
• There can be no more than **238 representatives** from the States and Union territories.
 
• The Fourth Schedule's regulations in this regard must be followed when **allocating seats** in the Council of States for representatives of the States and of the** Union territories**.
 
• The **method** of **choosing** the Union territories' representatives in the Council of States shall be **prescribed** by law by the **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is: *Article 80*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
 

 __**Article**__
 __**Description**__
 
 

 **Article 64**
 According to Article 64, the** Vice-President **is required to serve as the Council of States'** ex-officio chairman** and cannot hold any other lucrative positions.
 
 

 **Article 56**
 If the **President** resigns on his own or breaks the law, he may be removed from office. The President's tenure in office begins on the day he **assumes office** and lasts for** five years**.
 
 

 **Article 78**
 According to Article 78, it is the responsibility of the **Prime Minister** to **inform** the **President** of all decisions made by the Council of Ministers regarding the management of Union **matters** and legislative initiatives.
